column1: # Purpose: Define the complete dated worklist for the compiler coverage review.
# Responsibilities: Identify evidence, dependencies, implementation scope, and positive/negative acceptance cases.
# This file intentionally does NOT call missing behavior implemented or infer unknown runtime results.

column4: title
column6: current_behavior
column7: implementation
column8: positive_acceptance
column9: negative_acceptance

column4: Reject output aliases of compiler inputs and emissions
column6: Opening the sidecar truncates an aliased source before compilation; all three probes exit zero and yield an accepted empty END model.
column7: Stage output privately; validate file identity for all sources, includes, preincludes, and emission destinations before publication, including hardlinks and symlinks.
column8: Distinct output paths preserve input bytes and publish the expected nonempty module.
column9: Same path, relative alias, symlink, hardlink, include alias, and emitted-code alias cannot overwrite another artifact or report success.

column4: Check writes, close, and final publication
column6: PRINT and CLOSE are unchecked; /dev/full compilation exits zero without a write failure diagnostic.
column7: Centralize checked output, report failure to the driver, and publish the completed staged file only after successful writes and close.
column8: Successful publication yields a readable complete model with matching counts.
column9: Full device, short write, close failure, interrupted compile, and failed replacement never publish a newly complete model or silently succeed.

column4: Identify source revisions, encoding, and coordinate systems
column6: D contains paths only; records lack content identity, encoding/BOM, byte offsets, and a compiler build identity beyond the version string.
column7: Add file/revision identities, observed source digest or immutable revision key, encoding/coordinate declaration, and compiler build/config identity without rereading changed input as authoritative.
column8: UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, legacy bytes, BOMs, CRLF, and non-BMP characters map to the captured revision and documented columns.
column9: A changed file cannot be silently treated as the revision that supplied an editable semantic fact; malformed encodings remain noneditable.

column4: Export include occurrences and dependency relationships
column6: D deduplicates filenames; repeated include instances, parent includes, directive spans, include-once skips, preincludes, and outcome distinctions are lost.
column7: Give each include attempt/accepted source context an identity, parent, source event, requested/resolved file, ordinal, and actual outcome; retain unique dependency summary too.
column8: Repeated includes under different namespaces/configurations have distinct contexts sharing one file revision.
column9: Skipped, missing, or failed-open includes do not masquerade as successfully opened semantic contexts; skipped text receives no invented bindings.

column4: Export macro invocations, substitutions, and expansion origins
column6: Z/K describe definitions and retired macros; macro use sites, argument spans, parent expansions, substitution/stringify origins, actual callback output, and undef/redefine events are absent.
column7: Observe actual expansion once in the existing narrow/wide paths; publish invocation/argument/substitution/origin edges, expansion results, and definition lifetime events.
column8: Nested, variadic, multiline, stringifying, token-pasting, and callback macros trace each selected result to its invocation and definition.
column9: Do not reinvoke stateful callbacks, turn synthesized tokens into editable physical bindings, or emit recursion-suppressed names as ordinary calls.

column4: Record conditional compilation decisions and inactive regions
column6: Only accepted declarations survive; no #IF branch/condition/result/defined-use records or skipped source ranges identify why other text was inactive.
column7: Record conditional nesting, evaluated conditions, selected branch, defined-name uses, and skipped ranges as preprocessing events.
column8: Nested #IF/#ELSEIF/#ELSE and #IFDEF decisions retain the actual selected branch and context.
column9: Do not parse inactive code as semantic declarations, manufacture inactive overload targets, or evaluate skipped callbacks again.

column4: Record effective options and their source history
column6: Q captures target/CPU/language/backend and sizes, but omits most command-line and language options, OPTION/DEF policy, pragma stacks, reservations, and committed #CMDLINE changes.
column7: Capture the initial effective semantic configuration and ordered committed changes; attach context identity to source facts, including checking, FP, literal, mangling, array, keyword, and ABI defaults.
column8: OPTION BASE changes, DEF letter ranges, push/pop pragmas, EXTERN policy, #LANG, #CMDLINE restart, and per-module resets yield the expected contexts.
column9: Rolled-back attempts and popped options cannot leak into later facts; export must not enable options, checks, profiling, or debug information itself.

column4: Describe invocation, module role, and link inputs
column6: The stream has module paths without complete main/entry/output roles, source/object/preinclude inputs, search paths, library requests, target policy, or provenance of command-line defines.
column7: Export a normalized invocation/module manifest with explicit input classes and compiler-known library/search/output/entry choices, avoiding incidental process-private state.
column8: Multiple translation units, main selection, library attributes, #INCLIB/#LIBPATH, predefines, preincludes, and output modes retain their actual choices.
column9: Do not claim runtime-loaded libraries, linker-resolved addresses, or unavailable semantic bodies for prebuilt objects.

column4: Retain logical-to-physical source remapping
column6: #line sets a conservative nonphysical flag; logical filename/line metadata is not linked to the original physical source revision and remap event.
column7: Record remap events and both coordinate domains, preserving the current conservative editing policy unless a physical range is independently proved.
column8: Nested includes and repeated remaps preserve logical diagnostic coordinates plus the actual physical source origin.
column9: Remapped/generated coordinates never become editable merely because their logical filename resembles a dependency path.

column4: Capture source statements, compounds, and complete construct ranges
column6: N lines are zero without -g; even with debug markers there are no statement IDs, columns, colon-statement extents, complete declaration/body ranges, or source compound graph.
column7: Observe committed constructs in parser routes and carry source identity independently of debug nodes; record statement/block/declaration/procedure extents and structural roles.
column8: All declaration, compound, legacy single-line, colon-separated, continuation, include, and synthesized-body cases have documented source ownership.
column9: Enabling export cannot force -g or change emissions; generated statements cannot inherit false editable ranges from the nearest debug marker.

column4: Link typed source expressions and their lowered representations
column6: E stores typed range snapshots/prefixes without parent/operand/result edges; N stores later l/r trees without E-to-N identity, source context, or transformation lineage.
column7: Introduce source expression identities and semantic operand/owner edges before destructive folding/lowering; link surviving/generated N nodes and canonical type/value facts by phase.
column8: Nested expressions, folded expressions, operator calls, pointers, arrays, properties, conditional expressions, and cloned initializers retain source graph and lowering links.
column9: Do not infer expression parenthood from overlapping ranges, reuse pool addresses as IDs, or invent source AST operations for already-folded nodes.

column4: Cover every source operation route consistently
column6: IS/@/dereference/index can appear as E concepts without O records; CAST/CPTR/LEN/SIZEOF/NEW/DELETE lose source operation identity in this probe. Statement/intrinsic families have no uniform source event.
column7: Audit the finite source operation/statement dispatch vocabulary; observe selected built-in or overload semantics before folding/lowering, distinct from raw AST opcode.
column8: Every supported arithmetic, cast, address, member/index, type inquiry, allocation, mutation, string, memory, varargs, thread, console/file, graphics/sound, and error operation has a defined event policy.
column9: Do not classify identifier lookalikes, erased AST nodes, compiler helper calls, rejected overloads, or inactive macro text as source operations.

column4: Preserve declaration spelling, prototype names, and implicit declarations
column6: Named prototype formals have declaration B records but empty T names; an implicitly declared source variable is marked compiler and has only a reference B record. Original spelling and declarator roles are incomplete.
column7: Retain declaration occurrence metadata from the lexer, including supplied/omitted names, original spelling, source declarators, and explicit/implicit origin, without changing compiler symbol naming.
column8: Named and unnamed prototypes, body formals, implicit legacy variables, suffix declarations, aliases, and generated THIS parameters retain their distinct roles.
column9: Do not synthesize a written name for unnamed formals or label compiler temporaries as user declarations.

column4: Anchor constructor/destructor/operator declarations and definitions
column6: Special procedures have F/body metadata without source declaration bindings; the source operator in this probe is additionally reported with compiler origin.
column7: Observe special keyword/operator/type-designator sites as declaration occurrences with selected procedure identity, prototype/definition roles, and correct source origin.
column8: Constructors, complete/deleting destructors, conversion/binary/member operators, properties, and module constructors/destructors identify their written declarations and definitions.
column9: Do not create identifier bindings for an operator glyph or present generated special members as written declarations.

column4: Close alternate binding routes and distinguish semantic use roles
column6: The initial FutureType forward-name use has no B record even though its generated forward symbol and canonical target exist. B otherwise distinguishes only declaration/reference, without expression/call/type/access roles.
column7: Review every token-consumption route and attach selected symbol occurrences to source events, with roles for type use, read/write/address/callee/member/label and prototype/definition; preserve later canonical resolution.
column8: Forward references, aliases, qualified names, BASE/WITH members, function results, assembly BASIC symbols, varargs formals, labels, and overload selections resolve once to the correct symbols.
column9: Do not bind assembler-local names, unresolved recovery names, namespace lookalikes, keyword spellings, or indirect calls to invented procedure targets.

column4: Model source scope occurrences and ordered import visibility
column6: T lexical owner/lookup namespace, H imports, and U logical scope lines are present; reopening instances, USING directive ranges/order/lifetime, enum/anonymous scopes, and occurrence context are incomplete.
column7: Publish source scope identities/intervals and ordered namespace import/reopen/inheritance visibility events linked to the existing symbol owners.
column8: Shadowing, reopened namespaces, nested/anonymous types, scoped enums, imported namespaces, include instances, and out-of-line method bodies retain the actual lookup context.
column9: Do not conflate lexical ownership with lookup namespace or infer a new visible import outside its source context.

column4: Provide a stable normalized type and flag contract
column6: Resolved raw dtype/subtype, spelling, attributes, status, UDT flags, and primitive sizes are available; consumers still need compiler-specific bit layouts and promotion/remap/return-method policy.
column7: Define normalized type constructors, per-level const/pointer qualifiers, nominal/alias/signature identities, and stable named flags/ABI enums while retaining raw diagnostic fields.
column8: Pointers with qualifiers at every level, aliases, strings, enums, UDTs, procedure pointers, varargs types, mangle modifiers, and integer promotion policy normalize consistently.
column9: Do not treat distinct nominal types as identical based on spelling or erase fixed-string length/qualifiers; do not claim raw information already exported is absent.

column4: Separate natural alignment, packing request, and effective layout
column6: U uses the packing override instead of natural alignment when present, so both values cannot be recovered from that field.
column7: Export natural alignment, requested packing/override, and effective alignment separately, with finalized padded/unpadded sizes and existing field/bitfield positions.
column8: Packed/unpacked structs, unions, inherited and anonymous members, bitfields, arrays, and target-specific rules retain all distinct alignment values.
column9: Do not overwrite natural alignment with packing or assign layout to incomplete/forward types as if finalized.

column4: Complete compiler-known parameter and aggregate ABI classifications
column6: F exports ABI result dtype/method, G source mode/rank/body variable; formal BYDESC real subtype, register classification, and UDT retin2regs are absent. Source convention does not fully describe effective target ABI.
column7: Export frontend-selected real parameter type/descriptor and register/aggregate result categories with source versus effective convention; mark later backend-only classification as a separate optional phase.
column8: 32/64-bit source conventions, byref/bydesc/variadic/THIS, aggregate returns, register passing, wchar descriptors, and target FP options retain the actual selected classifications.
column9: Do not expose stale local pointers after flush or claim final stack/register locations before backend allocation.

column4: Relate virtual tables and RTTI storage to their types
column6: Default/copy constructors, destructors, copy assignment, override targets, virtual slots, and abstract count exist; owning-type vtable/RTTI storage relations and the complete table contract are absent.
column7: Add owning type to vtable/RTTI relationships, layout/count/slot semantics, and inherited entry origins; reuse existing special-member and overload relations where derivable.
column8: Inheritance, abstract methods, virtual overrides, RTTI identity tests, deleting destructors, and empty virtual tables retain compiler-known ownership and slot choices.
column9: Do not advertise a runtime dynamic dispatch target as known or infer table ownership solely from generated symbol names.

column4: Expose source mangling mode and emitted external identity
column6: T exports alias but not mangling mode or lazily produced link name; builtin declarations can be emitted as libc symbols by Clang/LLVM after the source snapshot.
column7: Record source linkage policy and compiler-selected emitted link identity when known, including target decoration and builtin-to-libc mapping, with explicit unknown/unavailable state.
column8: C/C++/Windows/rtlib aliases, namespace overloads, data exports, proc addresses, and builtin mappings identify the correct compiler-selected link symbol.
column9: Do not force code emission/mangling side effects during observation or invent linker addresses/resolutions for external declarations.

column4: Record declaration order, procedure status, and startup registrations
column6: Priority, FB_PROCEXT.stats, declaration statement numbers, label declared/GOSUB flags, global ctor/dtor membership/order, and wrapper-to-instance registration links are absent.
column7: Publish semantic declaration/action ordinals and procedure/label status with ordered startup/teardown registrations and priorities; retain existing bodies.
column8: Multiple priority levels, same-priority source order, branch-crossing declarations, GOSUB labels, result-assignment/RETURN usage, static and global instances retain selected metadata.
column9: Do not confuse FB_SYMBSTATS with FB_PROCSTATS or rely on export-ID allocation order as declaration/registration order.

column4: Retain compiler-observed literal intent and typing provenance
column6: C preserves exact resolved numbers/string units, but literal suffix, escape mode, original spelling/radix, and contextual typing/promotion provenance are absent.
column7: Attach lexical literal intent and selected type/value to source expression identities while retaining exact C encoding and distinguishing source values from generated constants.
column8: Signed/unsigned boundaries, suffixes, radix forms, negative zero/NaN/Inf where accepted, embedded NULs, wide units, and language-dependent literal types remain exact.
column9: Do not derive exact values from decimal pretty-printing, collapse wide units into host bytes, or attach a written suffix to a synthesized constant.

column4: Export initialized operator options and result-load meaning
column6: Raw opcode and some target relationships exist; initialization/pointer/coercion/inverted-branch options and LOAD.isres are omitted.
column7: Add class-validated stable payload properties for initialized operator options and result loads; use the correct union member for each producer.
column8: Initialization versus ordinary assignment, pointer arithmetic, inverse comparison branches, no-coercion paths, and result loads have distinct properties.
column9: Never read inactive/recycled union slots, especially ADDROF.ex and nonoperator conversion flags; reject impossible class/property combinations.

column4: Export inline assembly tokens, bound operands, and barrier contract
column6: N assembly nodes have only kind; B covers BASIC names separately, without ordered assembly text, operand-node links, or memory/register clobber/barrier contract.
column7: Serialize the actual ASTASMTOK text/symbol sequence and source ownership; expose the compiler's conservative assembly effect policy, with optional backend constraint details.
column8: Instructions with bound BASIC variables/procedures, local assembly labels, register names, newline boundaries, and backend clobber policy preserve actual tokens and operand identity.
column9: Do not treat register names/assembly-local labels as BASIC bindings or claim instruction-specific alias/effect knowledge the compiler does not possess.

column4: Complete initializer scope payload and ownership
column6: TYPEINI offsets/counts exist, but scope-begin/end offsets/bytes, matched initializer scopes, and semantic scope ownership are not complete.
column7: Serialize initialized scope payloads and matched scope/owner edges before merging/flushing, including array/UDT distinction and source-to-generated initializer lineage.
column8: Nested arrays/structs/unions, padding, bitfields, constructor lists, field defaults, and cloned/merged initializers retain valid offsets, sizes, and scope matching.
column9: Do not read elements as bytes for a constructor list, is_array from a TYPEINI payload, or uninitialized scope-end fields.

column4: Retain block, procedure, and source-exit structure
column6: The procedure/block wrapper itself is not traversed by ExportProc; block parents, entry/exit labels, statement intervals, ismain, and source break/exit ownership are not explicit records.
column7: Record source block/procedure identity and entry/exit/control relationships before break-list consumption; link lowered branches/cleanup to each source exit.
column8: Nested scopes, EXIT/CONTINUE/RETURN/GOTO/GOSUB, procedure main/module roles, and generated scope cleanup retain ownership and actual targets.
column9: Do not serialize private list/cursor addresses or reconstruct source exits solely from the final generated branch sequence.

column4: Preserve source DATA items and RESTORE ownership
column6: DATASTMT nodes are consumed into descriptor initializers; those initializers and values are exported, but source DATA item type/order/range and label-to-data ownership are not explicit.
column7: Record source DATA groups/items and selected RESTORE data target, linked to generated descriptor arrays; reuse existing lowered constant/initializer facts.
column8: Numeric/string/wide/NUL/address data, multiple groups, forward labels, READ targets, and RESTORE starting points retain source and runtime sequence meaning.
column9: Do not call the internal reverse C-emission list source execution order or manufacture a DATA AST node that no longer exists.

column4: Traverse deferred call actions outside ordinary child edges
column6: The exported copyback probe has one FB_STRASSIGN call, while emitted C has two. CALL.strtail source trees and profile begin/end trees are outside the l/r traversal.
column7: Give auxiliary call actions explicit typed/ordered edges and capture their symbols/trees before disposal, without moving execution; export final generated action origin links too.
column8: Fixed-string BYREF writeback, nested calls, multiple copybacks, profiling, result temporaries, and no-copyback ordinary strings retain all actual actions in order.
column9: Do not execute, duplicate, reorder, or falsely attribute a deferred action to a source callee occurrence.

column4: Represent semantic actions introduced after the export phase
column6: N precedes astLoad; check-handler transfers, USTRING indexed-read runtime calls, hidden argument/result handling, some profiling/bridge actions, and backend ABI helpers can be introduced later.
column7: Define explicit source/typed/lowered semantic phases and observe semantically relevant late actions/edges at their real creation point; separate backend-only instruction detail.
column8: Bounds/null/dimension checks, Unicode scalar read/write, varargs, hidden results, UTF-8 bridges, profile calls, and aggregate ABI helpers have documented origin/effect coverage.
column9: Do not claim a pre-load AST is the final executed action graph or alter lowering solely to make it observable.

column4: Model call-site arguments, defaults, conversions, and dispatch roles
column6: F/G and ARG.sym preserve signatures/formal links; source argument ordinal, supplied/default/implicit role, adaptation stages, call-site identity, and source versus helper-call lineage are incomplete.
column7: Introduce call-site/argument identities linked to formals, source order/ranges, chosen direct/indirect/virtual/intrinsic dispatch, default trees, conversions/materialization, and generated actions.
column8: Optional/variadic/instance/byref/bydesc arguments, overloaded operators/properties, virtual calls, proc addresses, THREADCALL, and temporary construction link to selected facts.
column9: Rejected overloads and unknown dynamic targets stay absent; do not equate ARG.mode=default with an omitted optional argument.

column4: Explain base/member initialization and implicit object operations
column6: Base/chained constructor calls and generated base/field/vptr initialization can exist in N, but the I vocabulary does not provide a complete reason/owner/source/action ledger for them.
column7: Link each compiler-selected object initialization/copy/destruction/vptr action to its owner, reason, source declaration or BASE/CONSTRUCTOR event, selected target, and order.
column8: Explicit/default base initialization, constructor chaining, field initialization, generated special members, union exclusions, copy/move-like materialization, and virtual-base-compatible semantics retain selected actions.
column9: Do not fabricate constructors for plain storage, duplicate compiler-generated calls as source references, or run mutually exclusive initialization paths together.

column4: Represent lifetime ownership, conditional cleanup, and destruction order
column6: I selects several implicit constructor/destructor kinds and ranges; it does not identify every emitted cleanup node, conditional temporary lifetime, cleanup sequence, wrapper registration, or owner/exiting edge.
column7: Publish lifetime/action identities for local/global/static/temporary/result/argument objects, initialization state/condition, ordered cleanup, and source exit/registration relationships.
column8: Conditional IIF/short-circuit temporaries, nested scopes, early exits, static guards, global teardown, arrays, returns, deleted objects, and cloned initializer temporaries retain correct lifetimes/order.
column9: No cleanup for unconstructed/borrowed storage, no unconditional cleanup for an unselected conditional temporary, and no stale identity after pool reuse.

column4: Expose semantic evaluation order and conditional execution
column6: N l/r traversal order is structural; calls evaluate argument chains before function-pointer expressions, and short-circuit/conditional/link nodes need class-specific execution semantics.
column7: Publish semantic sequence/conditional edges and source argument ordinals, derived from actual AST/lowering behavior with unspecified order explicitly marked where appropriate.
column8: Nested side-effecting arguments, indirect-call pointer expressions, all supported conventions, IIF/ANDALSO/ORELSE, LINK result edges, and cleanup actions preserve actual sequencing/conditions.
column9: Consumers must not assume DFS left-before-right or infer an order the language/compiler leaves unspecified; export cannot reorder execution.

column4: Provide a complete conservative control-flow graph
column6: Branches, labels, comparison targets, and J entries permit partial reconstruction; source compounds and late error-handler/GOSUB/indirect transfers prevent a complete graph from the present records alone.
column7: Build documented basic blocks and normal/conditional/case/return/indirect/error/resume/GOSUB edges after the required semantic phases, retaining source links and unknown-target sets.
column8: Loops, SELECT variants, early exits, legacy GOSUB/ON GOTO, indirect branches, checks, ON ERROR/RESUME, and unreachable regions retain correct edges and block membership.
column9: Do not invent fallthrough after unconditional transfer, mark dead branches executed, or resolve indirect/error targets without evidence.

column4: Add read/write, use-def, and escape relationships
column6: Symbol/type bindings alone do not expose read/write/read-modify-write roles, definition/use chains, address escape, or argument mutation/borrowing facts.
column7: Build access events and conservative use-def/escape summaries over the complete semantic graph; distinguish direct symbolic storage from uncertain pointer/descriptor aliases.
column8: Assignments, compound assignments, fields/arrays/bitfields, address taking, BYREF/BYDESC, returns, READ/INPUT, and known call bridges yield valid access relationships.
column9: Do not report every reference as a read or claim exact pointee aliases/definite initialization when the compiler has no such proof.

column4: Summarize compiler-known effects and preserve uncertainty
column6: The compiler has coarse side-effect/cloneability decisions and known runtime calls; there is no normalized memory/allocation/I/O/error/thread/barrier/termination effect model.
column7: Add conservative effect contracts for known AST operations/intrinsics and transitive procedure summaries with explicit unknown/conditional effects; preserve the compiler's existing optimization meaning.
column8: Known pure math, allocation/free, string mutation, file/console/graphics/sound, synchronization, error handling, profiling, END, and assembly retain appropriate effect categories.
column9: Unknown externals/indirect calls/assembly cannot be declared pure or assigned precise alias sets from their names; optional summaries must not change compiler optimization policy.

column4: Export structured diagnostics and their semantic context
column6: Errors/warnings go to text output; there are no code/severity/location/parameter/context/related-symbol diagnostic records in either model mode.
column7: Observe actual emitted diagnostics through the centralized diagnostic system, with physical/logical source/context links and stable code/severity, retaining existing display behavior.
column8: Syntax, lookup, overload, access, type/layout, warning, include, parameter, limit, and backend diagnostic paths yield consistent structured facts.
column9: Do not emit suppressed/discarded-attempt diagnostics as current ones, parse console text to infer semantics, or turn warning generation into extra compiler behavior.

column4: Attach validity and failure regions to provisional facts
column6: RECOVERY distinguishes an incomplete compact snapshot globally, but does not identify invalid/skipped/recovered constructs, synthetic replacements, affected expressions, or failed module reasons.
column7: Give module/source facts explicit committed/provisional/invalid/synthetic status and link diagnostics/skipped regions; define partial full-model policy deliberately rather than accepting an incomplete stream as complete.
column8: A bad middle statement with valid surrounding statements, multiple failed modules, restarts, missing includes, and recovered default expressions retain clear validity boundaries.
column9: Never present a compiler recovery placeholder as a proved user expression or an incomplete full model as semantically complete.

column4: Declare phase, capability, and completeness coverage explicitly
column6: END validates transport counts/transaction success, not every semantic family or all phases; footer totals cannot show a producer route that never emitted facts.
column7: Add explicit schema capabilities, phase coverage, per-module/family status and dropped/failure reasons, retaining count/integrity validation separately.
column8: Consumers can distinguish complete required families, intentional compact omissions, recovery, dependency truncation, and unavailable late/backend data.
column9: A zero-count missing family, overflow, ignored write, or failed producer cannot silently become a complete capability claim.

column4: Make snapshot phases, identity lifetimes, and cross-module ownership explicit
column6: IDs are valid within an invocation and canonical replacements exist; repeated T/F/G snapshots have implicit phases, M provides stream context, and E/N have no shared identity or explicit version/retirement ownership.
column7: Define invocation/module/source-event/symbol/node identity domains, snapshot phase/version and canonical retirement rules; correlate phases without requiring memory addresses or globally stable IDs.
column8: Multiple modules, prototype-to-body updates, forward patches, interned procptr formals, recycled symbols, and delayed/generated procedures preserve identity and phase ownership.
column9: Do not reuse a retired allocation identity, consume stale local pointers, conflate same-named external declarations across modules without linkage evidence, or promise stable IDs across different builds.

column4: Exercise payload semantics for every live AST and symbol class
column6: Vocabulary tests compare enum/name switches; payload assertions cover a subset of live classes. COMP has no constructed nodes and CLASS has no constructor in this source inventory.
column7: Use the class/field matrix to require behavior tests or a documented no-node/implementation-only disposition for each current class and field family, at the relevant phase.
column8: Each live class exercises its meaningful payload, relationships, lifecycle, values, and constraints with representative compiler-produced fixtures.
column9: Wrong active-union reads, absent required payload, impossible class/property pairs, unknown values, and fabricated nodes for enum-only classes are rejected.

column4: Cover every declaration, expression, statement, and intrinsic route
column6: 624 token case sites and common parser routes form a finite review inventory; current suite/corpus does not map every route to positive and exclusion assertions.
column7: Maintain a route-to-fact-to-fixture manifest covering source forms and alternate shared routes; classify internal-only opcodes rather than demanding all 122 AST opcodes as source syntax.
column8: Every source feature family and overload/special variant has required output assertions tied to intended semantics and source ownership.
column9: Malformed/inactive/ambiguous/access-denied/unsupported/lookalike variants emit no fabricated binding, target, layout, lifetime, or editable range.

column4: Cover target, dialect, backend, and semantic option interactions
column6: Tests cover selected Linux/Windows x86/x64 and GCC/Clang/LLVM/gas64 cases, not the complete feature/ABI/option interaction space or big-endian/non-x86 compilation metadata.
column7: Choose justified equivalence partitions for all supported language/target/backend policies; add compile-only cross-target metadata and selected executable integration cases.
column8: FB/fblite/deprecated/QB, 32/64-bit, little/big endian, wchar width, source/effective conventions, FP policy, checking, packing, varargs, and intrinsic availability are covered.
column9: Unsupported backend/target/feature combinations remain diagnostic outcomes with no false completeness; assert correct reset across modules and restarts.

column4: Prove observation preserves code, diagnostics, and language behavior
column6: Existing corpus checks compare emissions for off/full/compact, but new provenance, late-action, option, and effect families need equivalent noninterference coverage and diagnostic comparisons.
column7: Extend frozen-input comparisons across the gap fixtures and compiler-self/real-program corpus, including optimized/debug/checked modes and actual execution where meaningful.
column8: Off/full/compact select the same language decisions, warnings/errors, emitted code, and runtime results for valid programs across representative backends.
column9: Export must not reexecute macro callbacks, reselect overloads, change evaluation order, enable debug/check flags, or alter the output code to obtain facts.

column4: Exercise bounded failure, allocation, and publication contracts
column6: Dependency limits/pool reuse/interruption have some coverage; all record/buffer/signature/literal/stack limits, allocator failures, writer/close failures, and deep/repeated phase lifetimes do not.
column7: Add deterministic fault injection or test-configured small limits with cleanup checks, checked arithmetic, bounded traversal, and fail-closed publication/diagnostic assertions.
column8: Near-limit inputs, repeated modules/restarts/clones/deletes, and permitted deep trees complete with valid identity closure and no memory errors.
column9: Boundary overflow, OOM, null/corrupt internal contracts, full disk, close failure, interruption, and rejected alias publication leave no newly complete invalid model or leaked ownership.

column4: Validate semantic payload integrity beyond record totals
column6: Changing K node kind to pretend-kind or an argument byte count to nonnumeric is accepted with unchanged footer totals; required per-class payload and relation consistency are incomplete.
column7: Specify and validate per-kind property vocabulary/types/ranges/mandatory fields, legal relation domains, call argument closure, jump ordinals, constant/node coherence, and phase/context ownership.
column8: All legitimate producer records, repeated snapshots, canonical replacements, zero/unknown optional states, and extensible capabilities validate under the documented schema rules.
column9: Unknown/impossible kind, bad numeric payload, missing required property, class/type contradiction, invalid relation, omitted action, duplicate/conflicting snapshot, and corrected-total corruption are rejected as appropriate.

column4: Keep the compiler coverage manifest current and reviewable
column6: The new inventory and field rules account for the dated source surface, but text matches are not execution coverage or proof of future completeness.
column7: Integrate a maintained class/contract/route/capability/test manifest with review-required changes when compiler contracts, dispatch routes, semantic phases, or schema producers change.
column8: Every current field/route has a documented semantic disposition, evidence, required capability, and acceptance coverage or justified intentional exclusion.
column9: A new or changed class/payload/route cannot satisfy completeness merely by adding a name to a switch, a hook text match, or an untested fallback rule.

column4: Expose lookup and overload selection explanations
column6: Selected overloads and signatures are exported; candidates, conversion ranking, accessibility filtering, and rejection/ambiguity reasons are not a public explanation trace.
column7: Optionally observe actual resolver decisions and scores once, tied to the source call/context; keep candidates/explanations separate from selected binding and effect records.
column8: Ambiguity, inaccessible overloads, imported candidates, constructor/cast conversion ranking, default/variadic/BYDESC matching, and successful choice retain real resolver explanations.
column9: Never rerun resolution, expose discarded candidates as executed calls, or claim hypothetical candidates were actually considered.

column6: Frontend snapshots intentionally precede final registers/frame offsets/instructions/debug numbering and some ABI emission classification; these are not existing complete frontend semantic facts.
